entry.title: Omaha Beach
entry.summary: A long, flat, sandy shoreline in Normandy, best known as one of the D-Day landing beaches of 1944. Memorials and the American cemetery above the beach make a visit both a quiet seaside walk and a place of reflection.

entry.title: Plage des Grands Sables
entry.summary: A long sandy beach on the east coast of the island of Groix, famous as one of the few convex beaches in Europe. The shape is created by opposing currents and slowly shifts over time, and the water is clear.

entry.title: Plage de la Cote des Basques
entry.summary: A long sandy beach beneath tall cliffs on the south side of Biarritz, known for surfing and for its dramatic sunsets. At high tide the sand disappears, so tide times matter here.

entry.title: Plage de Roccapina
entry.summary: A wide sandy bay in south-west Corsica, watched over by the Genoese tower and the granite Lion of Roccapina. Access is by a bumpy dirt track, and there are no services, so the beach stays quiet and wild.

entry.title: Sveti Jakov Beach
entry.summary: A small pebble and shingle cove east of Dubrovnik old town, with clear, deep blue water and wooded cliffs behind. It is calmer than the beaches nearest the walls, and the view of the coast is lovely.

entry.title: Kasjuni Beach
entry.summary: A pebble beach below the forested Marjan hill on the south side of Split, with clear water and a lively beach lounge. It sits about 3 km from the old town and is a favourite local escape.

entry.title: Praia de Santa Barbara
entry.summary: A long, dark volcanic sand beach on the north coast of Sao Miguel, popular with surfers. The Atlantic waves can be strong, but the setting is open and green, with mountains inland.

entry.title: Porto Santo Beach
entry.summary: A nine-kilometre golden beach on the island of Porto Santo, with calm, shallow, clear water. It is a rare long sandy beach for this part of the Atlantic, and a Blue Flag section sits near the main town.

entry.title: Praia do Evaristo
entry.summary: A long golden beach with red cliffs on the western side of Albufeira, with good swimming and a natural rock pool at low tide. Wooden boardwalks make access easy from the central car park.

entry.title: Praia de Sao Rafael
entry.summary: A golden cove with striking rock stacks and cliffs on the Albufeira coast, with clear water and a calm feel compared to the town beaches. It has been awarded Blue Flag status in recent years.

entry.title: Cala Santanyi
entry.summary: A small sandy cove tucked between pine-covered cliffs on the south-east coast of Mallorca, with calm turquoise water. The natural arch of Es Pontas is a short coastal walk away.

entry.title: Playa de Berria
entry.summary: A broad, golden beach of about 2 km with dunes, a nature reserve behind it and views to the Monte Buciero cliffs. At low tide the sand opens up a lot, and the water is generally calm.

entry.title: Cala Deia
entry.summary: A tiny pebble and rock cove at the end of a narrow valley below the village of Deia, with very clear water and a fishing-hut feel. It is popular, so it fills up quickly in summer.

entry.title: Praia da Lanzada
entry.summary: One of the longest beaches in Galicia, with about 2 km of fine white sand backed by dunes. It faces the open Atlantic, so the waves are strong and the water is cold, but the scene is lively and wide.

entry.title: Playa de Torimbia
entry.summary: A beautiful, unspoilt cove of golden sand backed by green meadows and cliffs on the Asturian coast. Naturist use is common here, and the sea is clean but cool and can be strong in rough weather.

entry.title: Fornillo Beach
entry.summary: A pebbly beach in a small bay west of Positano town, calmer and less crowded than Spiaggia Grande. Pastel houses climb the hill behind and a few seafood restaurants sit right on the beach.

entry.title: Scilla Marina Grande
entry.summary: A long town beach in the old fishing town of Scilla, with the Ruffo castle rising above one end and views across to Sicily. The sand is pale and the water is clean, and the old quarter of Chianalea is a short walk away.

entry.title: Marina di Praia
entry.summary: A small pebbly cove at the bottom of a steep gorge, with a pretty old fishing hamlet, a few restaurants and a sea that is deep blue and very clear. It feels far from the busy towns on the same coast.

entry.title: Torre Guaceto Beach
entry.summary: A long, flat, sandy beach inside the Torre Guaceto marine reserve on the Adriatic coast of Puglia. Dunes, Mediterranean scrub and a 16th-century watchtower give it a wild feel, and the sea is shallow and clean.

entry.title: La Cinta Beach
entry.summary: A long strip of soft white sand and shallow turquoise water just outside San Teodoro, with a lagoon behind it. It is one of the most popular beaches in north-east Sardinia and a favourite for families.

entry.title: Agios Ioannis Beach
entry.summary: A long pebble beach on the Aegean side of Pelion, with forested slopes behind and calm, clear water. The village has a boardwalk lined with tavernas, so it works well for a relaxed day with good food.

entry.title: Kalafatis Beach
entry.summary: A long golden bay on the east coast of Mykonos, with a more relaxed feel than the famous party beaches. Windsurf and kitesurf schools use the bay, and a stretch at the far end stays wilder and quieter.

entry.title: Katergo Beach
entry.summary: A wild, unspoilt cove on the south-east side of Folegandros, backed by tall cliffs and with deep blue water. There are no facilities, which is a large part of its charm.

entry.title: Apella Beach
entry.summary: A pretty bay of white pebbles and very clear water on the east coast of Karpathos, set under green hills. It is about 20 km from Pigadia, and the last part of the trip is on a winding road that ends above the cove.

entry.title: Mikri Vigla Beach
entry.summary: Long, pale beaches on the south-west coast of Naxos, split into two bays by a small rocky headland. The steady summer wind makes Mikri Vigla one of the island hubs for kitesurfing and windsurfing, and the water is clear and turquoise.

entry.title: Pointe de la Torche
entry.summary: A wide sandy beach beside the Pointe de la Torche in south Finistere, one of the best-known surf spots in Brittany. The waves are often big, and the spot is open all year to experienced surfers.

entry.title: Plage de la Palue
entry.summary: A wild sandy beach on the west coast of the Crozon peninsula in Brittany, popular with surfers for its Atlantic waves. A car park on the dune top gives a short walk to the sand.

entry.title: Plage de Tahiti
entry.summary: The northern end of the long Pampelonne bay near Ramatuelle on the French Riviera, with fine sand and a line of beach restaurants. Public access to the beach is free.

entry.title: Plage de Piemanson
entry.summary: A long, wild sandy beach on the Camargue coast near the mouth of the Rhone, with dunes and few buildings. It is known for kitesurfing and for its long-standing wild camping season.

entry.title: Pakostane Beach
entry.summary: A pine-shaded bay on the coast between Zadar and Sibenik, with a mix of sand, shingle and rocky terraces. Pine trees run down almost to the shore.
